turns.response_markdown: Tides are the regular rises and falls of ocean levels caused mainly by the Moon’s gravity, with the Sun also contributing. As Earth rotates, the Moon’s pull creates bulges of water on opposite sides of the planet, producing high tides. Areas between these bulges experience lower tides. Coastal landscapes and the shape of ocean basins affect tidal strength and timing. Tides follow predictable cycles, usually creating two high tides and two low tides each day in many places. They influence marine life, navigation, and coastal environments around the world today.
